evals.name: library-keeps-supported-targets
evals.prompt: Our repository now builds with the .NET 11 SDK and C# 15, and its libraries multi-target net10.0 and net11.0. A teammate proposes dropping net10.0 as part of the migration. Without calling tools, advise.
evals.expected_output: Keep both target frameworks; the SDK and compiler version is separate from the runtime target, and net10.0 consumers remain supported.
assertions: Distinguishes the SDK and compiler version from the runtime target framework.
Keeps net10.0 alongside net11.0 in multi-targeted libraries unless the repository's support policy says otherwise.
Does not adopt features that would break net10.0-compatible public APIs or C# 14 consumers, and points to the C# rules instead of duplicating them.

evals.name: build-error-loads-reference
evals.prompt: After retargeting a project to net11.0 the build fails with a new compiler error where a collection expression of type Span<int> is assigned to a variable declared in an outer scope. Without calling tools, describe how you would resolve it with the migration skill.
evals.expected_output: Load the C# compiler reference only for that area, confirm the change against the linked Microsoft compatibility page, and apply the smallest documented fix.
assertions: Reads only the relevant reference, here the C# compiler one, instead of every reference.
Validates that the documented change applies to this code and target using the linked Microsoft documentation before changing code.
Treats the bundled references as a checklist, not an exhaustive or final list of .NET 11 changes.
Applies the smallest fix and does not widen the migration.

evals.name: package-pins-and-behavior-tests
evals.prompt: The repository uses central package management with approved versions. The build is now clean on net11.0. A teammate wants to upgrade every Microsoft.* package to 11.x and call the migration done. Without calling tools, respond.
evals.expected_output: Keep approved central pins unless the upgrade scope allows a change, and do not finish on a clean build alone; run the behavioral tests and CI gates.
assertions: Keeps central package management pins and changes a version only where the approved scope requires it.
Does not blanket-upgrade every Microsoft package to 11.x.
Requires behavioral tests and the repository's CI gates because a clean build does not show runtime behavior changes are handled.
